Discontinue when pregnancy recognized; LDL lowering not needed during pregnancy

summary: Bempedoic acid is an oral ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor that lowers LDL cholesterol by reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis upstream of HMG-CoA reductase. It is used to reduce LDL-C in adults with hypercholesterolemia (including HeFH) and to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in those unable to take statins. It is a prodrug activated mainly in the liver, sparing muscle, so it causes less myalgia than statins. Key risks are hyperuricemia/gout and tendon rupture.
indications: To reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization) in adults at increased risk who are unable to take recommended statin therapy
Adjunct to diet/exercise (alone or with other LDL-lowering therapy) to reduce LDL-C in adults with primary hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

dosage.n: Swallow whole; with or without food

dosage.d: 180 mg once daily, separated from sequestrant
dosage.n: Give >=2 h before or >=4 h after the sequestrant

admin: Take one 180 mg tablet orally once daily, with or without food
If used with a bile acid sequestrant, give bempedoic acid at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after
Analyze lipid levels 8 to 12 weeks after initiation
If a dose is missed, take it when remembered; do not double the next dose
moa: Bempedoic acid is an adenosine triphosphate-citrate lyase (ACL) inhibitor. It and its active metabolite require CoA activation by very-long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSVL1), which is expressed primarily in the liver. ACL lies upstream of HMG-CoA reductase in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway; inhibiting ACL decreases hepatic cholesterol synthesis and upregulates LDL receptors, lowering blood LDL-C. Because activation is largely confined to the liver, skeletal muscle is relatively spared.

absolute: History of a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., angioedema) to bempedoic acid or excipients
relative: History of tendon disorders or tendon rupture (avoid)
Concurrent simvastatin >20 mg or pravastatin >40 mg (myopathy risk)

preg: There are no adequate data on use in pregnancy. LDL-C lowering offers no benefit during pregnancy and may interfere with fetal development; discontinue bempedoic acid when pregnancy is recognized.
lact: It is not known whether bempedoic acid is present in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild or moderate renal impairment. There is limited experience in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease on dialysis - monitor for adverse effects.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment. It has not been studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment.

major: Simvastatin >20 mg (increased simvastatin levels; myopathy risk - avoid)
Pravastatin >40 mg (increased pravastatin levels; myopathy risk - avoid)
moderate: Other statins (monitor for statin-related adverse effects)
Bile acid sequestrants (reduced bempedoic acid absorption - separate dosing)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum uric acid, creatinine/BUN, and hepatic transaminases; may reduce hemoglobin/leukocyte/platelet counts

monitoring: Lipid panel (LDL-C) 8-12 weeks after initiation, then periodically
Serum uric acid periodically; monitor for gout symptoms
Signs and symptoms of tendon injury (pain, swelling, inflammation)
Liver enzymes and CBC as clinically indicated
counsel: Take one tablet once daily, with or without food, swallowed whole
Report joint/tendon pain, swelling, or inflammation - stop and seek advice (tendon rupture risk)
Tell your doctor about gout or high uric acid
Continue diet and exercise; this medicine adds to, not replaces, lifestyle measures
If taking a bile acid sequestrant, separate the doses as instructed
pk: LDL-C reduction develops over weeks; assess at 8-12 weeks
Plasma peak approximately 3.5 hours after dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C
pearls: Liver-selective activation (via ACSVL1) means skeletal muscle is largely spared - useful in statin-intolerant patients with myalgia
Inhibits renal tubular OAT2, raising serum uric acid - monitor and watch for gout
Tendon rupture is a recognized risk - avoid in patients with prior tendon disorders
Greater LDL reduction when combined with ezetimibe (available as a fixed-dose combination)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In the event of overdose, treat symptomatically and institute supportive measures as needed. Because of high plasma protein binding, dialysis is unlikely to substantially enhance elimination.
